purpose: Methods reference for future Iowa cancer models; no model fitted and no Iowa exposure effect estimated

sources.title: SEER*Stat: Calculating Age-adjusted Rates
sources.cancer_application: Compare standardized cancer rates while preserving the standard population and age groups
limits: Age-adjusted rate is not a count or personal probability
Do not reconstruct counts by multiplying by local population

sources.title: Appendix A: Statistical Considerations
sources.cancer_application: Construct demographic-specific expected cases and descriptive observed/expected ratios
limits: Reference choice changes interpretation
Uncertainty and comparison population must be reported

sources.title: Suppression of Rates and Counts
sources.cancer_application: Preserve suppressed small cells and distinguish from zero
limits: USCS suppresses statistics below 16 cases/deaths
Additional suppression and source-specific rules can apply
Do not infer confidential cells by subtraction

sources.title: Cancer Characteristics, Definitions, and Recent Investigations
sources.cancer_application: Prespecify same or etiologically related cancers, population, area and period
limits: Boundary changes can create/obscure apparent patterns
An association does not establish causation

sources.title: Phased Approach to Respond to Community Inquiries: Phase 3
sources.cancer_application: Assess feasibility and cancer-specific latency/residence histories
limits: No universal lag
Diagnosis address may not identify etiologic exposure location

sources.title: Modeling exposure-lag-response associations with distributed lag non-linear models
sources.source_type: original methods paper with simulation and cohort example
sources.cancer_application: Represent intensity and timing of historical exposures; radon/lung-cancer example
limits: Not a source of one transferable Iowa lag
Correlated histories and sparse outcomes can weaken identification

sources.title: Ecological bias, confounding, and effect modification
sources.cancer_application: Constrain interpretation of county exposure/cancer associations
limits: Aggregate control/standardization need not remove ecological bias
Group association cannot identify which individuals were exposed

sources.title: Causal Inference in Occupational Epidemiology: Accounting for the Healthy Worker Effect by Using Structural Nested Models
sources.authors: Naimi AI; Richardson DB; Cole SR
sources.source_type: methodological commentary with causal diagrams and original simulation
sources.cancer_application: Interpret occupational comparisons and work/health/exposure feedback
limits: General-population comparisons affected by selection

Method assumptions must be assessed

sources.title: Unbounded Discrete Distributions
sources.cancer_application: Model integer cases/deaths with appropriate log offsets and dispersion
limits: NB2 variance is mu + mu^2/phi
Dispersion alone does not model spatial dependence or confounding

sources.title: An intuitive Bayesian spatial model for disease mapping that accounts for scaling
sources.authors: Riebler A; Sorbye SH; Simpson D; Rue H
sources.cancer_application: Partially pool area risks with structured/unstructured county variation
limits: Smoothed risks are model-dependent
Spatial effects do not identify causal exposures

sources.title: Spatial Models in Stan: Intrinsic Auto-Regressive Models for Areal Data
sources.cancer_application: Implement constrained and scaled areal random effects
limits: ICAR prior is improper without appropriate constraints
Neighbor definition and priors affect estimates

sources.title: Bym2 model for spatial effects
sources.cancer_application: Check mixing/precision parameterization and connected-component behavior
limits: Confirm current implementation defaults
Mixing fraction is latent variance allocation, not attributable cancer fraction

sources.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
sources.cancer_application: Control false discoveries in prespecified exploratory families of county/cancer/exposure tests
limits: Original proof assumes independent tests
Multiplicity correction does not remove bias or establish causation

sources.title: Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure
sources.source_type: methods paper with simulations and case studies
sources.cancer_application: Choose spatial or forward-time holdouts matching the future prediction target
limits: General methodological evidence, not Iowa cancer application

sources.title: Posterior and Prior Predictive Checks
sources.cancer_application: Check count distributions, extremes, dispersion and interval behavior
limits: In-sample fit is not independent validation
Good prediction does not establish causation

sources.title: Measurement Error and Meta-Analysis
sources.cancer_application: Propagate exposure measurement/reconstruction error through an explicit observation model
limits: Latent exposure is not identified merely by adding a parameter

sources.title: Truncated or Censored Data
sources.cancer_application: Represent known detection limits instead of substituting zero for nondetects
limits: Censored and missing data are different
